The story

Founded in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, in 1892, the company first gained prominence for producing accurate pocket watches for the American railroads, earning the title "The Watch of Railroad Accuracy." The brand later became a key supplier of timepieces to the U.S. military, a legacy that continues in its popular Khaki Field, Khaki King, and Khaki Field Expedition Auto lines. Hamilton has a history of innovation, introducing the world's first electric watch, the iconic Ventura, in 1957, and the first LED digital watch, the Pulsar, in 1970. The brand's connection with Hollywood has seen its watches appear in over 500 films. Today, Hamilton is part of the Swatch Group and its watches, including the elegant Jazzmaster Open Heart Auto and the sporty Jazzmaster Performer, are Swiss-made, blending American design heritage with Swiss mechanical movements. The Intra-Matic Auto Chrono is a modern example of its classic chronograph designs. Manufacturing in the United States ceased in 1969, and the company's headquarters and production were moved to Biel, Switzerland. This move solidified its position as a Swiss-made brand while retaining its American spirit.
